PUBLIC HEARING

  1. TDA Article 8 Hearing
  The Metropolitan Transit Authority (MTA) is required to hold a public hearing on the
  community’s unmet public transit needs in accordance with the Transportation
  Development Act (TDA) Article 8. TDA Article 8 funds are currently being used by the City
  of Avalon to fund Avalon’s Consolidated Land Transportation Program which includes
  DAR and fixed routes.
  Recommended Action
  Open the Public Hearing and accept comments from the public. Close the Public Hearing.

ORAL COMMUNICATION
Members of the public may address the City Council at this time. No action will be taken on non-
agenda items at this meeting. Speakers should limit comments to two (2) minutes each.

PRESENTATION Finance Director Matthew Baker will provide an overview of the progress of

the FY 2021-2022 Budget.

CONSENT CALENDAR

1.  Minutes
  Although the live recording is the official record of public meetings, actions are prepared
  for the Councils approval.
  Recommended Action
  Approve minutes from the April 5, 2022 regular City Council Meeting.

2.  Warrants
  Expenditures Submitted for Approval
  o Warrants in the amount of S814198.67.
  o One payroll in the amount of Si 85,963.02.
  o Three electronic fund transfers totaling $104,143.85.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the disbursements for March 28, 2022 through April 8, 2022 totaling
  $1,104,305.54.

3.  Resolution of Support for LGBTQ Rights and Inclusion
  This item appears on the agenda at the request of a member of the City Council. The
  proposed resolution of support for LGBTQ rights and inclusion is a response to legislation
  that is currently being adopted throughout the nation. The proposed resolution supports
  legislation that creates a safe, supportive and accepting environment that promotes
  understanding and acceptance of all individuals inclusive of their sexual orientation,
  gender identity and gender expression.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution of support for LGBTO rights and inclusion.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
APRIL 5, 2022
PAGE 3

GENERAL BUSINESS

4.  First Extension of CR&R’s Franchise and Lease Agreement
  The City of Avalon entered into a Franchise and Lease Agreement with CR&R,
  Incorporated for solid waste, recyclables, green waste, C&D and debris box collection
  services and solid waste facility operation at the Pebbly Beach Landfill on March 20, 2013.
  The “Initial term” of the agreement was for the period commencing on July 1, 2013 and
  ending on June 30, 2023.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the first extension of the franchise and lease agreement with CR&R Incorporated
  for solid waste, recyclables, green waste, C&D and debris box collection services and
  solid waste facility operation at the Pebbly Beach Landfill.

5.  Upgrade Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant Process Air System
  The City’s wastewater treatment plant operator, Montrose Environmental reported that
  the aeration system that provides the air for the biological processes at the WWTP needs
  some repairs. The biological system requires a minimum air flow for normal operations.
  Without sufficient air the biological process breaks down, which causes an upset at the
  plant, which could lead to a process failure.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the procurement of supplies, equipment and services for the upgrade of the
  Avalon WWTP process air system for a not to exceed cost of S200,000.00.

Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of
California Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared
state of emergency wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or
recommended, the CITY OF AVALON’S CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING
COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL GENERALLY BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC
REMOTELY. The general public may attend the meeting in the Council Chambers
however must adhere to social distancing requirements. The public is encouraged to
watch and participate from the safety of their homes while practicing social distancing.

Council Chambers are open to a maximum 30 members of the general public. Once the
Council Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in
Oral Communication and address the City Council on an agenda item in person by
waiting in the City Hall Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time at the
appropriate time. No one will be admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or
exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. Additionally! the general public may participate in
Oral Communication and address the City Council on an agenda items by providing
comments via e-Comment. Please use the link below to provide comments via e

SUBJECT:  Resolution of Support for LGBTQ Rights and Inclusion

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt a resolution of support for LGBTQ rights and inclusion.

REPORT SUMMARY: This item appears on the agenda at the request of a member of the
City Council.

The proposed resolution of support for LGBTQ rights and inclusion is in response to legislation
that is currently being adopted throughout the nation. Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and
queer people in the United States face discrimination in their daily lives. While many
jurisdictions work to pass laws to protect LGBTQ people, others work to advance legislation
that targets transgender people, limit local protection and allow the use of religion to
discriminate.

Specifically, in 2022 more than 172 bills at the state or federal level have been introduced that
would target transgender and nonbinary people for discrimination by criminalizing healthcare
for trans youth, barring access to the use of appropriate facilities like restrooms, restrict trans
student’s ability to fully participate in school sports, and make it more difficult to get
identification documents with the correct name and gender.

The proposed resolution supports legislation that creates a safe, supportive and accepting
environment that promotes understanding and acceptance of all individuals inclusive of their
sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: N/A

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

  WHEREAS, the lack of awareness and understanding of issues facing LGBTQ+

ideations or attempts; and

  WHEREAS, education about and support of LGBTQ+ individuals increases

  WHEREAS, harassment and bullying policies that specifically mention sexual
orientation, gender identity, and gender expression are associated with: students and
employees feeling safer; lower levels of bullying; decreased incidents of harassment
related to sexual orientation; and a great reporting of incidents.

SUBJECT:  First Extension of CR&R’s Franchise and Lease Agreement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Approve the first extension of the franchise and lease
agreement with CR&R Incorporated for solid waste, recyclables, green waste, C&D and debris
box collection services and solid waste facility operation at the Pebbly Beach Landfill.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon entered into a Franchise and Lease Agreement with
CR&R, Incorporated for solid waste, recyclables, green waste, C&D and debris box collection
services and solid waste facility operation at the Pebbly Beach Landfill on March 20, 2013.

The “Initial term” of the agreement was for the period commencing on July 1 2013 and ending
on June 30, 2023. Per Section 3.6 of the agreement:

  “The Initial Term may be extended for two additional five-year periods (the “First
  Extension” and “Second Extension”). The First Extension and Second Extension shall
  take effect automatically on expiration of the Initial Term or First Extension as
  applicable, as long as the parties have not provided each other with at least one-year
  written notice of their decision not to execute the First Extension or Second Extension
  as applicable, for reasons attributable to the Company’s or City’s performance of the
  Agreement.”

The potential notification deadline to inform CR&R of the City’s intention to not automatically
renew this agreement is June 30, 2022.

CR&R has been a responsive contractor in the management of the City’s landfill operations.
Additionally, City Staff have relied heavily on CR&R for their expertise in navigating and
implementing the regulations associated with SB 1383.

City Staff recommend the City Council approve the First Extension of the Franchise and Lease
Agreement with CR&R. If the City Council does not approve the First Extension of the
Franchise and Lease Agreement, in addition to notifying CR&R of the City’s desire to not
extend the agreement, City Staff will begin the process of developing a Request for Proposals
(RFP) for qualified firms to fulfil the scope of work currently being overseen by CR&R.
 GOAL ALIGNMENT: Ongoing meeting of City obligations.

FISCAL IMPACTS: There are sufficient funds available, and the expenditures are included in
the FY21-22 Budget.

SUBJECT:  Upgrade Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant Process Air System

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the procurement of supplies, equipment and services
for the upgrade of the Avalon WWTP process air system for a not to exceed cost of $200,000.00.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City’s wastewater treatment plant operator, Montrose Environmental
reported that the aeration system that provides the air for the biological processes at the WWTP
needs some repairs. The biological system requires a minimum air flow for normal operations.
Without sufficient air the biological process breaks down, which causes an upset at the plant,
which could lead to a process failure.

The plant was originally built with five blowers which provided multiple efficient operation levels
to match the needs of various flow levels. One blower was removed from service in 2014 and a
second one was removed in March 2022, due to being at the end of their service life. These two
blowers are still at the plant and they were proposed to be rebuilt when taken out of service. The
three remaining blowers are not operating efficiently, and many of the operating combinations
of multiple blowers operating in tandem do not provide sufficient airflow to meet peak operating
conditions. The original aeration system design incorporated multiple redundancies so that if a
piece of equipment failed or needed servicing, other equipment could provide a safe level of
operation. The system developed problems during peak flows over the previous quarter and so
a full assessment was completed. It was found that the remaining blowers are nearing the end
of their useful life and need to be rebuilt or replaced as appropriate. With that finding it became
apparent that the system redundancy is becoming critically insufficient. A failure of the main
blower would require extraordinary process measures to continue operations. This is of
particular concern during the peak summer flows.

The aforementioned assessment considered two options from two blower vendors, which
considered operational efficiency, system redundancy and cost. Option A was the least cost
alternative and also the most efficient with motors rated at 10 HP less than the competing option.
These reduced HP motors along with the proposed installation of variable frequency drives will
deliver significant energy savings over time over option B and the current operation. Also
included in the upgrade are new actuators that will tie into the existing dissolved oxygen meters
to optimize the Dissolved Oxygen process.

The proposal has four components. The first is the purchase of three new blowers to replace
three of the five existing blowers, at an equipment cost of $89,818.00. One blower will remain
in operation and is proposed to be rebuilt in the future. The fifth blower will be scrapped for parts
for the blower that will remain in operation. The final configuration will now have four blowers
that will be sufficiently redundant to handle two failures before the system becomes critical. The
 second component is the programming of the integration of the blowers to the command and
control infrastructure of the plant at a cost of $12895.00. The third is the installation of new
actuators for automatic control of the air flow at an equipment cost of $21,479.82, The fourth is
the installation of the equipment including the electrical and mechanical trades. Some of this
work will be completed by Montrose or City staff. But, for work that will require outside forces a
contingency of $75,000 is requested. The estimated total cost of S199.192.82 is rounded up to
a not to exceed request of $200,000.00 for the project. The project is currently part of the capital
projects list for the plant, Capital Project #205012, “Major Sewer Projects’ is the annual funding
for an array of sewer capital projects on a prioritized basis. The project has sufficient remaining
funding to allocate to the project.

The work is exempt from the from the requirements of a public works project by the Public
Contracts Code and AMC section 3-4.201(d)(5) as it is sewer maintenance work at the City
owned WWTP. As previously stated, the project will be completed by Montrose and City staff
as the resources are available. These forces will be supplemented with licensed contractors
through competitive proposals as necessary to facilitate a timely and effective delivery of the
project.

For each of the four components, the procurement policies of the AMC are applied. Under the
first component (blower equipment) the AMC section 3-4.106(a) (vendor price quotes) was
utilized. Multiple contacts were made to seek at least three competitive quotes after a field visit
to view and assess the work. Three vendors responded, with two eventually submitting a
proposal. The selected proposal is attached.

For the second (programming) and third (actuators) components, the individual procurements
were under $25,000 so AMC section 3-4.102 was utilized. This does not require multiple
competitive quotes for this threshold but an evaluation of value was completed.

For the fourth component (outside contract labor), if any work is above the $25,000 threshold,
three competitive proposals will be utilized per 3-4.106(a). Otherwise the work will be through a
small negotiated contract(s) perAMC 3-4.102.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure reliability and safety.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Capital Project #205012 was approved by City Council in the 2021-22
budget and sufficient funding remains to implement the project

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The WWTP aeration
system will eventually fail.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Direct Montrose Environmental to procure the supplies, equipment and
services; and implement the project.

 1. BLOWER

  •  Positive displacement rotary blower for oil free atmospheric air
  •  Three-lobed rotors with ground profile, statically and dynamically balanced, made in nodular cast iron CS
  400-15 EN 1563
  •  Casing with integrated LOW PULSE devce for damping pressure impulses, reinforced with ribbing to
  eliminate distortions caused by loads and made in ngh strength grey cast iron G250 EN 1561
  •  Side-covers reinforced with ribbing to resist induced loads from shafts, made in high strength grey cast
  iron C 250 [N 1561.
  •  shafts integrated with rotors made in nodular cast iron CS 400-15 EN 1563 or coupled to rotors by means
  of forced coupling and key, made in steel C40 EN 10083/1
  •  Cylindrical Roller bearings for a calculated operating life of 100,000 hours at the maximum design speed
  and pressure conditions
  •  Maximum peripheral speed of the lobe head below 40 m/s (131.2 feet per second)
  •  Timing gears with helical toothed wheels and involute profile, hardened and grounded, made in steel
  •  16 Mn Cr5, coupled to the shafts by means of forced coupling with cone 1 50 and with pressurized oil
  mounting and demounting
  •  Two sets of Labyrinth seals on each shaft, without sliding parts and wear free with vent holes to limit the
  pressure inside the oil sumps
  •  Oil seal on each shaft, without sliding parts and wear free coupled with labyrinth seal to prevent the
  leaking of oil vapor into the air chamber of the blower
  •  Oil seal on the drive shaft by means of lip seal ring in high strength rubber (VITON) and hardened and
  ground shaft protection sleeve to ensure extended working life
  •  Lubrication of all bearings (drive side and gear side) and of the timing gears by oil bath with oil
  •  Splash disks locked onto the drive shaft
  •  Maximum blower speed <7000rpm, this implies low speed, ower friction and high efficiency.
  •  Standard aluminum data name plates

2. BASE FRAME

  •  Compact base frame supporting both the blower and the electric motor, integrated with patented
  •  Anti-vibration mounts capable of withstanding compression and shear loads with vibration damping level
  > 80%

  •  Can be supplied with integrated soundproofed enclosure

3. INLET SILENCER

  •  Silencer consisting of a section based on the principle of sound wave interference, adjustable according to
  the rotation speed of the blower, for the reduction of the sound energy emitted in the base frequency of

  2
   the compressor itself (below 500 Hz), and a second absorption section for the reduction of the sound
  energy emitted at frequencies above 500 Hz.
  .  Maximum pressure drop DP = 10 mbar (0145 psi = 4 inches of water column)

4. INLET FILTER

  •  Inlet filter integrated in the inlet silencer.
  •  Filter element, located downstream of the sound absorbng material of the inlet silencer, to prevent any
  contamination of the conveyed air and to protect the compressor.
  •  Patented tunable silencer feature to allow for on-site adjustment by operators.
  •  Efficiency of the filter element 93% for particles >= 10 micron
  •  Inspection hatch for easy replacement of the filter element.
  •  Maximum pressure drop with new filter element OP = 5 mbar (0.0725 psi=2 inches of water column)
  •  Maximum pressure drop with clogged filter element DP = 25 mbar (0.362 psi=10 inches of water column)

5. DISCHARGE SILENCER

  •  Discharge silencer consisting of diffusion and resonance sections providing a wide reduction range and
  without sound absorbing material in order to avoid contaminating the plant downstream to the
  compressor package.
  •  Silencer integrated with the base frame supporting both the compressor and the electric motor.
  •  Maximum pressure drop 30 mbar (0.435 psi = 12 inches of water column)

 6. CHECK VALVE

  •  Factory installed check valve on the outlet silencer to prevent the reverse rotation of the blower when
  stopping.
  •  Rubber (EPDM) coated clapper plate with r&nforced central core in steel, without articulation hinge and
  wear and maintenance free.
  •  High strength rubber for maximum operating temperature 12 = 150’C (302*F)

7. STARTING/SAFETY VALVE (PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE)

  •  Direct acting spring loaded safety valve fitted on the outlet of the discharge silencer installed upstream of
  the non-return valve (check valve) in order to limit the di’ferential pressure on the blower.
  •  Valve to feature Metal to metal seat seal surfaces (maintena’ce free)
  •  Maximum settable pressure 1000 mbar (14.5 psi)
  •  Maximum operatng temperature 150 ‘C (302’F)
  •  Weighted PRV is an external optional accessory

  3
 8. PIPING

  •  The blower and silencers are directly connected to each other with flanges, without connecting pipes so
  as to reduce overall dimensions and pressure losses.
  •  The valves are directly fitted onto the compact base frame which also works as discharge silencer with
  dedicated brackets, without connection pipes in order to reduce bulk and loss of pressure.
  •  Connection to the system pipes by means of flexible connectors (EPDM) fitted at the outlet nozzle of the
  discharge silencer to compensate the pipes thermal expansion and to reduce the vibration transmission.
  •  Flexible connector in rubber reinforced with fabric inserts and suitable for operation up to 2 bar and
  temperatures up to 150’C (302’F), held in position with pipe clamp straps.

9. V-BELT TRANSMISSION

  •  V-belts with (V) cross sections
  •  Service factor >= 1.4 on fitted power
  •  Belt tensioning device based on the motor weight with automatic compensation for the belt stretching
  and maintenance free.

10. MOTOR

  •  Asynchronous three-phase electric motor with squirrel cage rotor constructed in compliance with NEMA
  standards.
  •  High efficiency motor suitable for operation with 460 V, 200 V 230 V, or 575 V +1- 10% and 60Hz +/-2%
  supply. As well as options for 380V-SOHZ & 415V-SOHZ.
  •  Minimum protection grade P54
  •  Cooling system TEFC casing cooled with external fan on the shaft.
  •  Assembly arrangements IM B 3 or NEMA F3 location (with terminal box at the top).
  •  Insulation class F
  •  Over-temperature class B
  •  Minimum service factor 1.15
  •  Drive side bearing to support the radial load induced by the V-belt transmission.
  •  Optional accessories include PTC thermistors and Space heaters, specified at time of order.

11. SOUND ENCLOSURE

  •  Hood made up of modular self-supporting panels, 18GA steel, powder-coated.
  •  Optional weather hood shields available. Territory sales managers can discuss specific site applications
  when needed if units are to be installed in extreme conditions.
  •  Seal between panels by means of special rubber joints to ensure airtight closure in order to allow outdoor
  installation.
  •  Sound-absorbing material consisting of open cell polyurethane foam thickness 50 mm (2”) with profiled
  finish, fire resistant according to ISO 3795 (MVSS TN 302)

Subject: 2022 Blower update proposal

Dear [Avalon City Council].

  We have recently Completed an assessment of airflow for the Waste Water Treatment Facility
Aeration system. The assessment indicates that the Aeration blower performance has continued to
degrade. The blowers, installed circa 1973: are still producing sufficient air flow for site operations.
However, the assessment indicates that there is no remaining spare or backup capacity. A single
point of failure would lead process upsets and potential non-compliance. Were this to occur, the site
team would balance air-flows to mitigate compliance risk. We strongly recommended executing this
project in expedited fashion.

  Attached are ASAs required for replacement and upgrade of the Waste Water treatment site
Blower systems. We have provided our recommendation as Option A, and have also provided an
alternative Option B.

  The recommended replacements are lower cost than the alternative option, and also provide
more value. In particular, the Option A upgrade includes VEDs that are comptible with other
equipment in Avalon treatment system. Further, Option A blowers are 10 HP less, and in combination
with the VFD technology, these will reduce Avalon energy costs over both Option B and existing
equipment. The recommended path allows for future optimization of the process Dissolved Oxygen
by tying existing DO meters into the new actuators. A summary of costs for these options is below.

SUBJECT:  Upgrading Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant process air system

  RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  integrating the VED controls to the existing flow meter. This will optimize
  site energy cost.

  • Remove existing #2 blower from service

  o #3 blower position

  • Install 1st new Gardner Denver blower in this position

  • Scrap existing #4 blower

  • Scrap blower

  • The channel blower is unaffected by this recommendation

Replace the existing actuators on each aeration basin to control the dissolved oxygen content
to each basin. These valves will work hand in hand with the DO probes in the basins, the PLC
and the new blower equipment.

  will provide minimum required air flow.
  • #1 blower
  • (new) #2 blower & (new) #3 blower
  • (new) #2 blower & (new) #4 blower
  • (new) #3 blower & (new) #4 blower
  • The system would be sufficiently redundant to handle any (2) failures.
  • Current system as it operates is running at max RPM’s while the new system
  is not only smaller in HP but able to regulate its output based on demand
  minimizes use of electricity.

REPORT SUMMARY: System Status

  •  The biological system requires a minimum of 650 SCEM at 6-7 PSI for normal
  operations.
  •  Overall, a failure of the #1 blower would require ‘extraordinary’ process measures
  to continue operations. This is of particular concern in the summerftourist
  seasons when plant loading is at a high point.
  •  Currently minimum flow can be accomplished with the following
  o #1 blower operating by itself
  •  Currently the following combinations do not create sufficient flow for normal operations
  o #2 blower operating by itself
  o #4 blower operating by itself
  o #1 blower and #2 blower
  o #1 blower and #4 blower
  o #2 blower and #4 blower
  •  Currently the following blower positions are out of service
  o #3 blower was removed in March of 2022
  o #5 blower was removed in —2014
  •  Currently, the following blowers could be considered for rebuild.
  o #2 blower.
  • It is possible after rebuild that it would match #1 blower performance and
  be able to provide minimum flow to site.
  • It is not recommended to rebuild this blower.
  If rebuild path is considered, this blower is best option. (2) new
  blowers would still be required.
  o #3 blower.
  • This blower is 75 HP, provides less flow than the existing 40 hp blower at
  a higher energy cost, and does not meet minimum flow requirements.
  • It is not recommended to rebuild this blower.
  o #4 blower.
  • This blower is 75 HP, provides less flow than the existing 40 hp blower at
  a higher energy cost, and does not meet minimum flow requirements.
  • It is not recommended to rebuild this blower.

  o  #5 blower.
   •  This blower was removed from service in/prior to 2014, it is still physically
  onsite.
  •  Rebuild is not a plausible option.

 1.  BLOWER

  •  Positive displacement rotary blower for oil free atmospheric air
  •  Three-lobed rotors with ground profile, statically and dynamically balanced, made in nodular cast iron CS
  400-IS EN 1563
  •  Casing with integrated LOW PULSE device for damping pressure impuses, reinforced with ribbing to
  eliminate distortons caused by loads and made in high strength grey cast iron 6250 EN 1561
  •  Side-covers reinforced with ribbing to resist induced loads from shafts, made in high strength grey cast
  iron C 250 EN 1561.
  •  Shafts integrated with rotors made in nodular cast iron 65400-15 EN 1563 or coupled to rotors by means
  of forced coupling and key, made in steel C40 EN 10083/1
  •  Cylindrical Roller bearings for a calculated operating life of 100,000 hours at the maximum design speed
  and pressure conditions
  •  Maximum periphera’ speed of the lobe head below 40 mIs (131.2 feet per second)
  •  Timing gears with helical toothed wheels and involute profile, hardened and grounded, made in steel
  •  16 Mn Cr5, coupled to the shafts by means of forced coupling with cone 1 50 and with pressurized oil
  mounting and demounting
  •  Two sets of Labyrinth seals on each shaft, without sliding parts and wear free with vent holes to limit the
  pressure inside the oil sumps
  •  Oil seal on each shaft, without sliding parts and wear free coupled w:h labyr9tb seal to prevent the
  leaking of oil vapor into the air chamber of the blower
  •  Oil seal on the drive shaft by means of lip seal rng in high strength rubber (VITON) and hardened and
  ground shaft protecuon sleeve to ensure extended working life
  •  Lubrication of all bearings (drive side and gear side) and of the timing gears by oil bath with oil
  •  Sp:•ash disks locked onto the drive shaft
  •  Maximum blower speed <7000rpm, this implies low speed, lower friction and high efficiency.
  •  Standard aluminum data name plates

2. BASE FRAME

  •  Compact base frame supporting both the blower and the electric motor, integrated with patented
  •  Anti-vibration mounts capable of withstanding compression and shear loads with vibration damping level
  > 80%

  •  Can be supplied with integrated soundproofed enclosure

3. INLET SILENCER

  •  Silencer consisting of a section based on the principle of sound wave interference, adjustable according to
  the rotation speed of the blower, for the reduction of the sound energy emitted in the base frequency of

  2
   the compressor itself (below 500 Hz), and a second absorption section for the reduction of the sound
  energy emitted at frequencies above 500 Hz.
  •  Maximum pressure drop DP = 10 mbar (0.145 psi = 4 inches of water column)

4. INLET FILTER

  •  Inlet filter integrated in the inlet silencer.
  •  Filter element, located downstream of the sound absorbing material of the inlet silencer, to prevent any
  contamination of the conveyed air and to protect the compressor.
  •  Patented tunable silencer feature to allow for on-site adjustment by operators.
  •  Efficiency of the filter element 93% for particles >= 10 micron
  •  Inspection hatch for easy reo.acement of the filter element.
  •  Maximum pressure drop with new filter element OP = 5 mbar (0.0725 psi=2 inches of water column)
  •  Maximum pressure drop with clogged filter element DP = 25 mbar (0.362 psi=10 inches of water column)

5. DISCHARGE SILENCER

  •  Discharge silencer consisting of diffusion and resonance sections providing a wioe reduction range and
  without sound absorbing material in order to avoid contaminating the plant downstream to the
  compressor package.
  •  Silencer integrated with the base frame supporting both the compressor and the electric motor.
  •  Maximum pressure drop 30 mbar (0.435 psi = 12 inches of water coiumn)

 6. CHECK VALVE

  •  Factory installed check valve on the outlet silencer to prevent the reverse rotation of the blower when
  stopping.
  •  Rubber (EPDM) coated clapper plate vjith reinforcec central core ir. steel, without articulation hinge and
  wear and maintenance free.
  •  High strength rubber for maximum operating temperature T2 = 150’C (302’F)

7. STARTING/SAFETY VALVE (PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE)

  •  Direct acting spring loaded safety valve fitted on the outlet of the discharge silencer installed upstream of
  the non-return valve (check valve) in order to limit the differential pressure on the blower.
  •  Valve to feature Metal to metal seat seal surfaces (maintenance free)
  •  Maximum settable pressure 1000 mbar (14.5 psi)
  •  Maximum operating temperature 150 ‘C (302’F)
  •  Weighted PRV is an external optional accessory

  3
 8. PIPING

  •  The blower and silencers are directly connected to each other with flanges, without connecting pipes so
  as to reduce overall dimensions and pressure losses.
  •  The valves are directly fitted onto the compact base frame which also works as discharge silencer with
  dedicated brackets, without connection pipes in order to reduce bulk and loss of pressure.
  •  Connection to the system pipes by means of flexible connectors (EPOM) fitted at the outlet nozzle of the
  discharge silencer to compensate the pipes thermal expansion and to reduce the vibration transmission.
  •  Flexible connector in rubber reinforced with fabric inserts and suitable for operation up to 2 bar and
  temperatures up to 1SOT (302’F), held in position with pipe clamp straps.

9. V-BELT TRANSMISSION

  •  V-belts with (V) cross sections
  •  Service factor >= 1.4 on fitted power
  •  Belt tensioning device based on the motor weight with automatic compensation for the belt stretching
  and maintenance free.

10. MOTOR

  •  Asynchronous tnree-ohase electric motor with squirrel cage rotor constructed in compliance with NEMA
  standards.
  •  High efficiency motor suitable for operation with 460 V, 200 V 230 V, or 575 V +1- 10% and 60 Hz +1-2%
  supply. As well as options for 380V-5OHZ & 415V-SDHZ.

 •  Cooling system TEFC casing cooled with external fan on the shaft.
 •  Assembly arrangements IM B 3 or NEMA F3 location (with terminal box at the top).

 •  Over-temperature class B
 •  Minimum service factor 1.15
 •  Drive side bearing to support the radial load induced by the V-belt transmission.
 •  Optional accessories include PTC thermistors and Space heaters, specified at time of order.
